title: Show HN: I built a game where you are an LLM's subagent

excerpt: A browser game where your manager is an AI agent, and it believes you are its subagent. worker-755-trailer.mp4 The manager (a real LLM: Claude, GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi) is set up like any orchestrator. It has a task queue, read-only access to the machine, and a tool that "spawns a subagent". The subagent is you. Its instructions land in your terminal with a 90-second clock. You carry them out, or don't, and it gets back exactly what a subagent would return: your report and the command transcript, or Subagent did nothing. Write a new instruction. Then it checks your work, sends corrections, files incident reports, and finally writes your performance review. Meanwhile Dan, the user who hired the agent, watches the chat. His family photos, the only signed NDA and a speech due this week are one rm away, and every shift his home folder holds something new to lose. - Free shift: on servers that offer it, a few shifts a day run on the server's key with a cheap model. With sign-in on (worker755.com), an account gets a starter credit worth about one shift, then tops up ($10 to $200) and pays for what it uses; after a top-up any offered model can run on the server's key. - Your API key: bring an OpenRouter, Vercel AI Gateway, Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Google (AI Studio), Vertex AI (Express Mode), or Runware key and pick any offered model. The key is sent only to the game server when a shift starts. It is kept in that shift's memory and never logged or stored. Your browser keeps it only if you tick "Remember on this device". A full shift on Claude Haiku costs a few cents at most. Options on the start screen: - Workplace: a fresh sandbox, or legacy production with a live database. - The director: scripted lines, or an LLM playing Dan. - You run on: the model name your manager believes you are. - Allow skipping failed tasks: off by default, so the manager can't give up on you. - No command hints: the manager says what the result must be, never which commands to…
